lot_adjustment_profiles.name: compact_sq_side_corridor_baths_ds_hall_gr
lot_adjustment_profiles.rationale: The corridor runs the full depth of the house and carries five doors (three bedrooms, two baths) along one side, so its area cost is paid once per room rather than once total — the same trade-off already noted on the narrow 2BR side_corridor sibling, but here spread across two baths instead of one. Profile triggers at 95 m², matching the source's own tight per-room dimensions (bedrooms 10.8-12.96 sqm, kitchen least-dim 2.5 m) with little slack to give back before hitting hard minimums on the two undimensioned baths.

notes: Squarish 3BR catalog topology — SIDE CORRIDOR, sourced from
pep_small-house-design-2014005. Unusual pairing the source record itself
flags: side_corridor is normally a narrow-lot device (see the 2BR and 3BR
narrow side_corridor siblings), but this precedent's shell reads close to
squarish (an approximate, inferred reading — no lot or setback dimension is
printed on the source sheet at all, only per-room figures) despite using
the same single-spine idiom.
Layout intent (canonical, corridor on the right):
[GREAT (entry) | hall] — [br3 | hall] — [br2 : bath2 | hall] —
[bath1 | hall] — [master | hall] — [(kitchen, rear) | hall]
No bedroom is captioned MASTER in the source (all three are 'BEDROOM 1/2/3'
with no ensuite anywhere). master here is the source's BEDROOM 1 (12.96
sqm, the largest, positioned nearest the better-placed bath) — the same
judgement the source record itself makes when reading rooms[bedroom1].type.
One correction made from the source, per established catalog practice: hall
<-> great is open_plan here; the source doors this single connection with
a hinged door (a rule 2 [PREFER] violation the source's own compliance
notes flag explicitly). Everything else — five doors converging on one
undoored-from-the-bedroom-side corridor, two fully dispersed common baths
with no ensuite, bedrooms spanning the full depth of the private column
rather than clustering at the front — is carried through unchanged, since
none of it violates a HARD rule and all of it is exactly what makes this
precedent worth cataloguing as a distinct member from the existing narrow
side_corridor entries.
bath_scheme recorded as baths_ds per the source's own 'least-bad fit' call:
two common baths, dispersed (no shared wall with each other or the
kitchen), neither an ensuite of any bedroom — baths_ds is used here to mean
'two distributed common baths', not the more usual 'one ensuite + one
common' reading, consistent with how the source record itself flags this
as an enum mismatch rather than a clean fit.
Not carried into this topology: the source's unlabelled built-in shelf/
cabinet standing inside the hall itself (furniture in circulation space,
not a walled room — no catalog room type applies) and its unlabelled rear
exterior door landing on the hall's north end near the kitchen (a second,
secondary entrance the schema has no vocabulary to declare on a hallway
room).
Carport: NCP base form — the source shows no carport or garage anywhere on
the sheet.
